tag: Sprint 14 Task E, F117 (F114 cloud read)

qcp-definition: Abstract p.1: the paper defines QCP as the term it builds on, read with Introduction p.2-3.
scope-limited-circuit-family: Section 1 p.3: the authors state that the method's benefits come at the cost of a limitation on the applicable circuits.
angle-encoding-qubit-requirement: Section 2.2 p.4 states the paper's own handling (split p features into subsets of at most m); the linear qubit requirement is the stated consequence of one-feature-per-qubit encoding in Section 1 p.2-3.
coefficients-scale-exponentially: Section 2.2.2 p.5: the paper states that the full construction still needs one coefficient per n-qubit Pauli string, so 4^n coefficients, and says how to cut it.
vqe-restricted-global-unitary: Section 2.3, Eq. 11, p.6: the paper defines the restricted form of V and shows unitarity in one line; the unitarity requirement is stated in the quoted text.
unitary-2-design-assumption: Section 2.4 p.8 and Appendix A p.17: the paper states as an explicit assumption that each subsystem circuit resembles a unitary 2-design, citing McClean et al. [21] for deep random circuits. This states the assumption, not a proof that the ansatz meets it.
measurement-error-accumulation-limit: Section 2.4.3 p.10: the authors state that their reasoning neglects accumulated measurement errors across subsystems.
ising-vqe-setup: Section 4.1 p.12-13: Adam, learning rate 0.1, 200 steps for every system, compared with exact diagonalization of Eq. 18.
digits-setup-simulation: Section 3.2.1 p.11: binary task of digits 3 and 6, 8-qubit simulation, 8x8 images that would need 64 qubits.
digits-model-parameter-counts: Section 4.2 p.13: 240 and 156 trainable parameters, 400 epochs, Adam at 0.1, MSE loss.
barren-plateau-experiment-setup: Section 4.2 p.14-15, Fig. 6: 2 subsystems of 8 qubits grown to 64 qubits, 20 random initializations, gradient w.r.t. the first parameter of the first subsystem.
generalizability-not-assessed: Section 5 p.15: the authors say they would like to test diverse systems and datasets to assess generalizability, so it is not yet assessed.
noise-not-tested: Section 5 p.15: the authors say they would like to investigate performance in the presence of noise akin to current devices; all results are noiseless simulations.
three-architectures-gat-schnet-mixed: Section II p.2 and Table I p.3: GAT, linear SchNet and mixed SchNet.
training-datasets-large-and-small: Section II.A p.2-3, Table I: 230.000 linear H4 instances, and 1.000 linear H4 plus 2.000 random H6 instances.
training-set-purposes: Section II.A p.3: the purposes of the two training sets are stated as design intent, not as results.
data-generation-pipeline: Section II.A p.3: the five-step data generation procedure with SPA circuit and VQE-obtained energy and parameters.
random-coordinates-constraint: Section II.A p.3 prose: each atom 0.5 to 2.5 A from the previous atom, minimum separation 0.5 A. Note Algorithm 1 samples a displacement dmax*u from a random earlier atom, so it is not worded identically; the value reports the prose.
bond-lengths-and-angles-regression: Section II.B p.4: the task is defined as regression because the angles (range -2pi to 2pi) are continuous.
zero-shot-fixed-variable-evaluation: Section III p.6: the evaluation protocol and baseline are defined.
random-instance-evaluation-setup: Section III.A p.6: 500 samples for each size 2,4,6,8,10,12, run through SPA optimization with the edge heuristic.
structured-instances-setup: Section III.B p.7: linear and ring Hn molecules, bond length from 0.5 A to 4.0 A, coordinates from Algorithms 2 and 3. The value leaves the upper end unstated; it is not wrong.
limit-hydrogenic-size-simulation-cost: Section I p.2: evaluation up to H12, limited at this time by simulation cost.
limit-minimal-basis-hydrogenic-next-step: Section IV p.8: extension to organic molecules in more accurate bases is named as the next step, so it is not shown.
limit-vqe-label-quality-global-minimum: Section IV p.8: the authors say VQE solution quality (global minimum is hard to find) can be improved. The passage is in the outlook; it implies the labels may not be global minima.
more-expressive-circuit-designs-grander-: Section IV p.8: adopting more expressive circuit designs is called a grander challenge that remains.
spa-definition-pair-product: Appendix B p.12: SPA is described as the approximation that the wavefunction is a product of electron pairs.
spa-orbital-rotations-not-in-circuit: Appendix B p.12: orbital rotations are not in the circuit and are optimized classically.
schnet-head-and-mixed-angles-per-pair: Section II.B.2 p.5 and II.B.3 p.6: original SchNet cut after the interaction blocks with a custom head; one angle per electron pair.
bincoletto-evaluation-setup: Section II.A p.3: evaluation datasets of 500 random instances, H2 to H12, minimal basis (one orbital, two qubits per H atom). Matches the stored value.
bincoletto-scope-hydrogenic-only: Section II.A p.3: the work focuses on hydrogenic systems because they are relatively simple to treat. Matches the stored value.
blanchette-guiding-principles: Section 2.2.2 p.6: the three guiding principles are listed.
blanchette-software-focus-rationale: Section 2.1 p.3: the degree focuses on quantum software, with the stated reason that physics and engineering programs cover hardware.
blanchette-timeline-2019-2022: Section 2.1 p.3: work began in 2019, program launched fall 2022.
blanchette-central-question: Section 1 p.3: the guiding question and the 2019 start are stated.
blanchette-output-profile: Section 2.2.1 p.4: the program aims to train quantum programmers who map practical problems to algorithms.
blanchette-entry-knowledge: Section 2.2.1 p.5: the paper states the input profile of entering students that the program design assumes.
blanchette-development-team: Section 2.2.3 p.6: three part-time resources over two years, plus an expert committee consulted periodically.
blanchette-career-paths: Section 2.3 p.7: three career paths the program is designed for.
blanchette-three-mandatory-internships: Section 2.3 p.7 and Figure 1: three mandatory work terms and professional development courses.
blanchette-math-courses: Section 3.1 p.9 and Figure 1: four math courses in semesters 1 to 3, and a tailored real analysis course in semester 5.
blanchette-physics-courses: Section 3.2 p.9: six physics courses; classical mechanics, waves and modern physics, and EM omitted because covered in CEGEP.
blanchette-qm-course-redesign: Section 3.2 p.9: first QM course redesign, spin-based, quantum computing perspective, tunneling and wells in the last two weeks.
blanchette-qm2-course: Section 3.2 p.9-10: the second QM course topics and its difference from traditional QM II.
blanchette-cs-courses: Section 3.3 p.10: six CS courses, Python first semester, four core courses, mandatory theory of computation.
blanchette-shared-cohorts: Section 3.4 p.10: some exclusive courses, most classes join existing cohorts.
blanchette-integrative-projects: Section 4.3 p.12-13 and Figure 1: five integrative project courses, team projects from three weeks to a full semester.
blanchette-ip-quantum-programming: Appendix 2 p.18 (BSQ101): four three-week projects; SAT with Grover given as an example.
blanchette-ip-quantum-solutions: Section 4.3 p.13 (two 6-week projects) and Appendix 2 p.18 (BSQ201: first iterations had a QML project and a neutral-atom adiabatic project).
blanchette-coop-structure: Section 4.4 p.13: co-op structure; internships at least 30% of the program.
blanchette-internship-schedule: Section 4.4 p.13 and Section 4.2 p.12: first internship after semester 4; second and third combined after semester 5; the 8-month internship is named in Section 4.2.
blanchette-final-semester-electives: Section 4.4 p.14: 12 credits of electives in the final semester.
blanchette-program-committee-changes: Section 5.2 p.14-15: the program committee meets at least once a semester; some courses were removed, replaced or moved after student feedback.
blanchette-program-aim: Abstract p.1: the program aims to train quantum software developers in three and a half years. Matches the stored value; this is the stated aim, not a result.
qaoa-layer-definition: Section 1 p.3: the paper states what a QAOA layer consists of, as the building block it reviews.
qaoa-approximation-ratio-definition: Section 1 p.3: the approximation ratio is defined as C_QAOA/C_max, the metric used in the review.
review-scope-and-aim: Section 1 p.3: the aim and the stated motivation (conflicting opinions in the literature) are in the paper's own statement of scope.
review-own-experiments-scope: Section 4.2 p.47-48 and Table 5: six QAOA variants (own implementations), MaxCut graphs of 4 to 18 nodes, 78 graphs, ongoing study.
review-own-experiments-optimizer-setting: Section 4.2 p.48: COBYLA, tolerance 0.0002 or 500 iterations, 1 to 8 layers, random initialization except WS-QAOA.
review-own-experiments-hardware: Section 4.2 p.48: IBM Falcon r5.11H processors ibm_oslo, ibm_lagos, ibm_nairobi, ibm_perth.
review-own-experiments-ma-qaoa-iteration: Section 4.2 p.48: the authors state the cap affected ma-QAOA and that unconstrained runs are planned.
review-own-experiments-limits: Section 4.4 p.52: the authors state what the curated results leave out and what is planned.
open-problem-noise-advantage: cross-group consistency, Rule B (coordinator, 2026-10-30): Review, Sec. 5.4 'Open Questions and Future Directions', p.61: the item records a question the review itself poses in its own list ('What is the prospect for quantum advantage of QAOA in the presence of noise and errors?', with the analysis it calls for). Recording that a review poses a question is own-voice about its own content: g088 Anshu Q01-Q25 and g090 qlt-open-* items of the same shape are graded high, scope. Siblings left low on purpose: open-problem-ogp-quantum-advantage asserts 'it therefore remains an open question' as a conclusion drawn from cited results [176, 192], a field-status claim; open-problem-parisi-value bundles Basso et al.'s cited conjecture [176].
qgrid-project-scope: Section 1 p.1: the project is a 3-year BMBF-funded project awarded in 2021.
qgrid-project-goal-nisq: Section 1 p.1-2: the stated project goal.
qgrid-four-approaches-scope: Section 1 p.2: four approaches for sub-problems of two use cases, described by background, formulation and benchmarks.
qgrid-dsp-definition: Section 2 p.2 and 2.1: the Discount Scheduling Problem and its main goal are defined.
qgrid-dsp-proportional-response-assumpti: Section 2.1 p.2: the central assumption of the formulation, with Eq. 3.
qgrid-dsp-constraints: Section 2.1 p.3: constraints named in general terms, details deferred to [4].
qgrid-dsp-metrics: Section 2.2 p.3: the three metrics are defined.
qgrid-dsp-solvers-compared: Section 2.2 p.3: Gurobi baseline, Leap, and own decomposition routine with named variants.
qgrid-dsp-gurobi-hardware: Section 2.2 footnote 1 p.3: M1 MacBook Pro (2020), Gurobi 9.0.
qgrid-dsp-parameter-settings: Section 2.2 p.3: elasticity set to one, five discount categories up to 50%.
qgrid-cd-divisive-algorithm: Section 3.1 p.5-6: the divisive greedy algorithm with K = 2, repeated recursively.
qgrid-cd-dynamic-weights: Section 3.1 p.5: adjacency weights computed dynamically from the power flowing through a line.
qgrid-cd-benchmark-instances: Section 3.2 p.5: pandapower IEEE cases adapted to residential grids, two shifted normal distributions, 50% producers.
qgrid-cd-benchmark-protocol: Section 3.2 p.5-6: five instances per case, lambda 0.1, Louvain for K, five runs per solver, 6 s and 3 s timeouts.
qgrid-csg-isg-approximation: Section 4.1 p.7, Eq. 8: the paper's own approximation of the CSG by an ISG with pairwise weights from a least-squares problem.
qgrid-p2p-formulation: Section 5.1 p.8-9, Eq. 16: the paper's own P2P auction formulation and its objective.
qgrid-p2p-benchmark-setup: Section 5.2 p.9: pandapower cases, largest has 39 prosumers, Gurobi, SA and QSA, 1000 reads, 10 runs, 30 s maximum.
qgrid-p2p-price-not-respected-limit: Section 5.2 p.10: the authors state that the formulation does not respect the energy price.
qgrid-utility-needs-more-study: Section 6 p.10: the authors state that further investigation is needed to find evidence of potential quantum utility. Matches the stored value, which is the caveat clause only.

theory_low.decomposition-into-subsystem-products: Eqs. 2 to 5, Section 2.1, p.3-4: an algebraic derivation in running text, not a stated and proved theorem. The quote is a fragment that drops the conditions (V expanded in Pauli strings with unitarity-preserving coefficients).
theory_low.expectation-values-polynomial-in-n: Section 2.2.2 p.5: shown by an inline bound (S*4^ns = n^(2*beta+1)/(beta*log2 n)) for equal-size subsystems with ns = beta*log2(n); not a stated theorem, and the quote ('One can show...') drops the conditions.
theory_low.vqe-expectation-values-constant-in-n: Section 2.3.2 Eq. 14, p.7: an inline counting argument that depends on the non-commuting Pauli-string construction described in the text; not a stated and proved theorem, and the quote drops the construction conditions.
theory_low.vqe-subexponential-expectation-values: Section 2.3.2 p.7: a worst-case count argued in running text; not a stated theorem; the quote is cut mid-sentence.
theory_low.local-terms-variance-scaling: Appendix A.2 p.18: E[(B)^2] = 1/(n^beta+1)^K is computed from the 2-design integral, but only under the unproven assumption that the paper's circuits are 2-designs. Not a stated theorem; the quote is a fragment.
theory_low.vqe-coefficient-scaling: Section 2.4.2 p.9: a worst-case calculation with c drawn uniformly; the paper's own result is E[d d*] = O(1/n^(3 beta)), an inverse polynomial, so the value's wording 'scales polynomially' is loose. Not a stated theorem; the quote drops the formula.
theory_low.subsystem-gradient-scaling: Section 2.4.3 p.10: an argument that builds on McClean et al. [21] and states no conditions as a theorem; the authors' own reasoning.

requote.blekos-qaoa-general-advantage-open-quest: regraded LOW at the team lead's decision: Section 5.1 p.54: this is the review's synthesis of the literature (classical solvers competitive, advantage an open question), the authors' interpretation, not a limit on their own experiments. Certainty change for the team lead: the passage does not state it as scope or a limit of this work.

value_replace.blekos-qaoa-general-advantage-open-quest: The review concludes that classical solvers remain highly competitive across a wide range of optimization problems and that a general and definitive quantum advantage with QAOA remains an open question.

blekos-qaoa-general-advantage-open-quest: classical solvers remain highly competitive in solving a wide range of optimization problems, making it challenging to achieve quantum advantage with QAOA.
Therefore, attaining a general and definitive quantum advantage with QAOA remains an open question.
